comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C24-C30 regarding tmFRET methodology. Both evaluations find these theoretical and methodological principles well-established and supported. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as a technological advance and strength of the manuscript.

Perfect agreement on claims C48-C49 regarding oligomerization effects on conformational equilibria. Both evaluations support these findings, though OpenEval notes the mechanistic interpretation in C49 is somewhat speculative while peer reviewers do not challenge it.

Perfect agreement on claims C59-C61 regarding cGMP producing the same structural states as cAMP but with different populations. Both evaluations find the phasor plot evidence compelling and consistent with prior structural data.

Perfect agreement on claims C76, C79-C80 regarding the capabilities and validation of time-resolved tmFRET. Both evaluations recognize this as a clear technological advance with unique advantages for measuring conformational heterogeneity and energetics.

Strong agreement on claims C52-C56 regarding time-resolved FRET data demonstrating ligand-dependent lifetime changes. OpenEval also addresses C57 (distance measurements), which peer reviewers implicitly accept by noting agreement with predicted values from structures.

Both support claims C17-C19 regarding electrophysiology data showing differential responses to cAMP versus cGMP. Peer review R1 also addresses main findings C5-C6, which OpenEval evaluates separately in R23.

Strong agreement on claims C70, C72-C73 regarding ionic strength effects. OpenEval also addresses C69 (SEC data) which peer reviewers implicitly accept. Both find the selective effect on cGMP activation clearly demonstrated.

Both support claims C31-C34 regarding donor/acceptor label incorporation. Peer review R2 also addresses C36-C39 (tetramer formation), which OpenEval evaluates separately in R8. Both acknowledge rigorous methodology.

Both support claims C36-C39 regarding tetramer formation and characterization. Peer review R2 also addresses C31-C34 (label incorporation), which OpenEval evaluates separately in R7. Both find the protein engineering rigorous.

Both support claims C40-C43 regarding steady-state FRET data. Peer review R3 also addresses C46-C47 (cGMP intermediate FRET), which OpenEval evaluates separately in R10. Both find results consistent across FRET pairs.

Both support claims C63-C65 regarding state populations from global fitting. Peer review R6 also addresses C66-C68 (energetic calculations), which OpenEval evaluates separately in R17. Both find the quantitative measures excellent.

Both support claims C66-C68 regarding energetic calculations based on state populations. Peer review R6 also addresses C63-C65 (population estimates), which OpenEval evaluates separately in R16. Both accept the thermodynamic analysis.

Divergent evaluations on claims C83-C85. OpenEval finds these limitations and theoretical considerations appropriately acknowledged and supported. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing that the relationship to full-length channels remains unclear and represents a significant limitation.

Both support the main findings C5-C6 regarding large structural changes and energetics. Peer review R1 also addresses C17-C19 (electrophysiology), which OpenEval evaluates separately in R4. All reviewers find the data compelling.
Both support claims C46-C47 regarding cGMP showing intermediate FRET efficiency. Peer review R3 also addresses C40-C43 (steady-state FRET with cAMP), which OpenEval evaluates separately in R9.

Divergent evaluations on claims C81-C82. OpenEval finds these claims about fragment activation supported by data. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting this as part of the broader limitation that detailed energetics are limited to the truncated construct.

Divergent evaluations on claim C74 regarding mechanistic interpretation of ionic strength effects. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature without additional structural data. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED without challenging the interpretation.

Both support claim C57 regarding distance measurements. OpenEval evaluates this separately while peer review R4 addresses it together with C52-C56 (time-resolved FRET data). Both note agreement with computational predictions.

OpenEval supports claim C45 (Hill slope observation) as part of steady-state FRET results. Peer review R10 addresses C45 in context of fragment versus full-length comparison, rating as UNCERTAIN due to limitations of using isolated fragments.
